DODGY DEVELOPER - THE STEWART GROUP

By: Nicky Troll | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A convicted fraudster rakes in millions of rands for residential developments that never seems to materialize leaving clients out of pocket and their home owner dreams shattered - are we dealing with

Summary:
From Jeffery’s Bay to Kuruman to Bloemfontein and most recently Pretoria – Erigh Stewart’s victims are out of pocket and furious – they were promised modern residential developments – parted with hundreds of thousands of rands and were left with half built property and some with land if they were lucky or worst case scenario – they get sweet nothing.

His cons allegedly range from duping home buyers to scamming potential investors to even forging bank documents to get payouts his clients will be held liable for.

We uncover Erigh Stewart’s trail of dodgy deals.

Further information:
I have a list of 39 people that have lost over R18 million to Erigh Stewart plus an additional 21 people still to contact that have had run ins with the Stewart Group.

I’ll call everyone personally and make a list that we can reference in the piece.

UNDERCOVER
I’ve got 40 minutes of undercover footage – I posed as an interested buyer. Erigh explains he’s had troubles with some developments, contractors and problem clients that have harassed him – at the end he turns on me realizing I was filming him and he intimidates me.

He traced my number plate and sent three threatening messages:

“Nice try now it is my turn”
“Hope you enjoyed your little film that you made”
“Hi Nicolene Celest Troll i think it is very sad that you pretend to be a client while working for Cart Banche .My family was harrassed by various people fake facebook pages and profiles.It is your job to find stories but i will take this matter up with legal council as the one woman already have a harassment order and open criminal case against her.”

THIS IS HIS MO – HE INTIMIDATES AND LETIGATES.

We approached Erigh for interview, I got Devi to call him – we recorded the audio. He basically says it’s smear campaign but he’ll consult with his lawyers – we then received a legal letter saying he won’t do an interview because of my underhanded behavior.

THIS IS NOT AN ISSUE – it’s like he declined an interview at the end. We have him on camera in the undercover, we also have a confront style interview with Standard Bank related to one of the case studies.

PRETORIA DEVELOPMENTS DRAMA
1. CLUB WILLA
- NO HOUSES, JUST A WALL AND GUARD HOUSE
- PREVIOUS HOUSE FLATTENED – ORIGINAL OWNER MRS DE BEER STILL BELIEVES SHE’ll GET A NEW UNIT… SHAME…

2. CORNER BESEMBESSIE STREEET & DR SWANEPOEL ROAD
- SOME BUILDINGS, NOT FINISHED
- LEGAL CASE WITH LAND OWNER – AT VAN WYK

3. STELLA STREET
- SOME HALF BUILT BUILDINGS, NOT FINISHED
- LEGAL ISSUE WITH LAND OWNER – PROPERTY HAS NOT BEEN TRANSFERRED, LAND OWNER LIVES IN CONGO.

4. DAWN STREET (FLEISCHMAN CASE)
- HALF BUILT BUILDINGS, NOT FINISHED
- VDH HAVE INSTITUTED BUILDER’s LIEN AGAINST PROPERTY
- LAND OWNED BY CLIENTS

5. MARAIS STREET
- GOT HOUSES – BUT NOT COMPLETE, NOT IN LINE WITH PLANS – OWNERS HAD TO PAY OTHER CONTRACTORS TO COMPLETE
- 3 UNITS OWNED BY INDIVIDUALS, FOURTH UNIT WAS SIGNED OVER TO VDH CONSTRUCTION IN LIEU OF PAYMENT FROM ERIGH

6. FLROENCE RIBEIRO AVENUE
- MR MAYNARD, A PENSIONER, WAS PROMISED A UNIT IN EXCHANGED FOR HIS LAND – HIS HOUSE WAS FLATTENED AND HE PAID IN R450k TOWARDS THE NEW UNIT TO BE BUILT ON HIS LAND – HE HAS NOTHING
- NO STRUCTURES AT THIS TAGE – JUST A WALL AND A GUARD HOUSE

7. THE EMBASSY
- NO STRUCTURES, JUST WALL
- ONE CLIENT, TEUNS WILLEMSE RECENTLY GOT HIS MONEY BACK

***** I HAVE PHOTOS OF ALL PROPERTIES – WE CAN GO VISIT SOME OF THESE TO GET FOOTAGE.

CASE STUDIES
I intend on using three cases – all with strong legal arguments – two have already won their cases in court.

1. ALLEN BRITTON
Allen Britton invested R1 450 000 with a promised return of R900 000 – they had a contract – Erigh was in breach – Allen took him to court and won – he has a court order for R2.5 million against Erigh from September 2018 – Erigh is meant to make monthly installments – he hasn’t.

2. CHRIS FLEISHMAN
2016 – 2017 transaction – still on going – still no property.

Bought land at Dawn Street in Lynwood – the amount was R2450 000 – this would include the land and the building of the house. R900 000 for the land – R1 550 000 for the building. The Fleischman’s signed the loan withdrawal with the bank for the R900 000 for the land which has been transferred on their name. After this – there were four withdrawals against the Fleischman’s Standard Bank loan – THEY DID NOT SIGN THESE WITHDRAWAL – THEY SAY THEIR SIGNATURES WERE FORGED. STANDARD BANK CAN’T PRODUCE THE ORGINAL DOCUMENTS.

The building is half built, what is there doesn’t match the plans that were approved and lodged with the bank – so in any case the bank the should not have signed off and allowed the payments to go through. The roof is incorrect and illegal in terms of Lynwood building regulations, the windows that have been installed are alos incorrect. STANDARD BANK HAS SOME EXPLAINING TO DO.

Currently Standard Bank are demanding bond payments from the Fleischman’s for a property that is not complete and illegal.

In addition, the construction company VDH Construction have instituted a builder’s lien claim against the property – Erigh put the Fleischman’s property down as collateral with the construction company – they have now instituted a claim agains the property.

This has happened to the other three unit owners at Dawn Street as well. Niel Joubert legally challenged Standard Bank and won – but signed a non-disclosure agreement – the bond was cancelled.

3. VDH CONSTRUCTION
This company has also won a case against Erigh – the result was that he had to sign over one of the units in one of the only developments that he completed – all be it not according to plan and there was work outstanding that the home owners had to foot the bill for. There was a quantity surveyor that testified against Erigh in this case and was received death threats afterwards.

ADDITIONAL INTEVIEWS
- GROUP LEADER
The person Erigh mentions he has the harassment order against is an estate agent who worked on marketing one of the developments and loaned him R280k – she and her husband realized something was not right and started warning clients. She has dug up a lot of history on Erigh and would be great as a hidden identity interview (pending her harassment case) to give a bigger picture of the extent of Erigh’s alleged fraud. She traced cases back to 1996.

- STANDARD BANK
- NHBRC – Erigh has undervalued a lot of the properties and they have had multiple complaints about him – but appear to not do much….
- Maybe a legal expert – to comment on the challenges with pursuing him criminally because he changes companies regularly – and the cases are dealt with individually on a civial bases and are not getting addressed criminally. I think it might actually be better to leave out the Group leader and just do the lawyer.

Script:


STRUCTURE VO: Buying property is one of the biggest investments you’ll ever make – financially and emotionally – but buying off plan often comes with added challenges. LINK: Developers can be charming and convincing – they sell you a dream, but sometimes all you get is a construction disaster and a never-ending nightmare. VO: This story is about one of these developers. Erigh Stewart. He currently operates as The Stewart Family Group, formerly HVARTSKA DEVELOPERS – his latest projects are in and around Pretoria and his pitches are said to be impressive and believable. But once you’ve signed on the dotted line and parted with your money – it seems to be a different story according to a string of unhappy clients. CHRIS: he still didn’t give me what I wanted JOUBERT: he has no conscious in terms of who suffers CASSELS: The mistake we made is trusted mr stewart VO: Neill and Mariaane Cassells bought a unit in one of Stewart’s upmarket developments in Marais street, Brooklyn at R2.8 million for the land and construction. CASSELLS : The plans were nice, the pictures he showed us were nice, we thought this could be our dream home VO: We sent in an operative with a hidden camera to meet the man behind the developments and to hear his sales pitch for ourselves. UPSOUND UNDERCOVER: ERIGH: Our building process is three months from start actual building to completion. // I make money on it – giving a product that nobody can give at that price, it’s a big house. VO: But as the delivery date neared for the Cassels, building was behind schedule and Stewart demanded more money. CASSELLS : // the house was nowhere near finished – so, I didn’t pay, I said there’s no house, no payment. // the contract says that at the stage of completion then you pay. UPSOUND UNDERCOVER: ERIGH: There’s a lot of clients complain this builder did this, the developer did this, // VO: But in the Cassells’ case it was more about what the developer didn’t do. CASSELS: Kitchen not done, has been started, //no red brick, no guttering, we had our own electrician come and test the system – we found 5 plug not earthed,// the geyser was not earthed. LINK: The Marais Street owners were lucky – despite the headaches, they got a mostly finished property – here at Dawn Street – just over R2 million a pop – all the owners have to show for it. DEVI: what’s it like looking at this? JOUBERT: it’s heartbreaking, it’s heartbreaking and knowing that this is actually worth nothing VO: Neil Joubert bought into this development – this is what he expected – and three years later – this – is what he got. JOUBERT: contractually we agreed upon a pitched titled roof //the roof was wrong, it wasn’t according to plan, //– in the title deed it says that you may not construct a chromadeck roof. VO: Besides the roof - experts found that there were serious structural issues resulting in cracks in the foundations and structures. JOUBERT: // The house was built outside of SANS tolerances – which meant that the whole structure was void and couldn’t be signed off by an engineer VO: Joubert took the matter to arbitration and won – he was awarded just under R1.7 million rand because the house needs to be demolished. More than a year later, Stewart has not paid a cent. Joubert’s neighbour, Christian Fleischman is in the same boat - except he claims, that Stewart fraudulently put through three payment requests totalling just over R650 000, against his building bond with Standard Bank. Those payments were over and above the first building claim Fleischman actually signed – the amount was just over R215 000 . DEVI: Who’s signature is on those documents? CHRIS: I don’t know// I only signed one form, I didn’t sign the rest. VO: We had a forensic handwriting analyst look at the signatures. The three signatures on the payment requests submitted to the bank by Stewart’s company – are in fact forgeries according to the handwriting expert. Andrew van der Hoven is head of Home Loans at Standard Bank. DEVI: // my question is how do you as the bank pick something like this. ANDREW: You will see that the signatures are very similar. But the point is we don't have handwriting experts looking at them. Unfortunately INT2 M9 // we would pick it up in the phone call. VO: Fleischman did receive a call from the bank to authorise. CHRIS: The person who called us from the bank asked if they should proceed to make payment, they didn’t ask if we are the ones who submitted the claims, that is two different statement DEVI: proceed with payment – you said yes CHRIS: I thought maybe it was related to the first payment, //, I didn’t know they were actually receiving other progress payment requests. DEVI: Where does this leave the Fleischmans? ANDREW: Unfortunately F still release the payment and in the final call still Confirm the previous payments made. VO: Fleischman is still liable for the entire bond and interest. But it’s not just unsuspecting home buyers who Stewart allegedly leaves out of pocket – some sub-contracts claim they were not paid. OCKERT: Part of his MO is to stretch as a contractor and not pay you at the end. VO: Ockert van den Heever’s company VDH Construction did work for Stewart on multiple sites – while payments were forth coming at first, it dried up and the company was owed over R4 million rand at one time. OCKERT: // – we all basically took a hit because we didn’t get paid by Stewart and his company. VO: In a letter to the Dawn Road owners - Stewart seemingly placed the blame on VDH – but the company was never responsible for structural work on this site – the accusations included fraudulent invoicing and bad workmanship - allegations Van den Heever strongly denies. Stewart also questioned VDH’s registration with the national home builders registration council. OCKERT: it was never a requirement in any one of our contracts.// We are commercial contractors// He can // try to badmouth us – but the fact is he didn’t pay. UPSOUND UNDERCOVER ERIGH: We heard all these rumours, and everybody said stuff, and I said prove it and nobody could prove it. VO: Suspecting that we were filming him, after 40 minutes, Erigh closed the door and confronted our operative. UPSOUND UNDERCOVER: ERIGH: Nicky, Where are you from? VO: After our operative left, Stewart sent these messages: Subsequently, we made multiple attempts to interview Stewart – telephonically and by email. UPSOUND DEVI:….we really want him to do the Interview. VO: In the end, he declined an on-camera interview and refused to answer questions in writing stating the information related to a harassment-matter currently in court . He also ironically accused us of being underhanded. While Erigh Stewart was convicted of fraud and theft in the nineties, we tracked down 36 people that were owed over 17 million rand by Stewart and his associated companies from Bloemfontein to Jeffery’s Bay and Pretoria. Attorney Hennie du Plessis has consulted with some of Stewart’s upset clients and sub-contractors. dEVI: are we talking who does have a def criminal MO - HENNIE: yes –same Mo is being followed // he signs agreements – never preforms in terms of agreement DEVI: Many companies – complicate thinks HENNIE: it doesn’t matter which entities is that - // if you lift the corporate veil who are you going to find – mr erigh stewart. VO: But it appears Stewart is also in the business of threatening those who challenge him. CASSELLS: //he publically said I will kill mr cassells. UPSOUND UNDERCOVER: ERIGH // I am not the forgiving kind of person – when you slander, when you steal from me // when I am ready then I will bite, VO: Stewart also has a reputation for litigating – Van den Heever believes it’s a stalling tactic, but his company was up for the fight. OCKERT // he knows when you go into a fight it’s going to take a long time or you might give up during the course of the fight – which we never did // we basically won every single one of those cases – so he then had to settle with us – which he also never did in full. VO: Stewart signed over a property worth just over R3 million rand to VDH – he still owes around R1.2 million in related costs . But business seems to be booming with multiple developments on The Stewart Family Group’s website on offer. LINK: Erigh stewart secures prime property for his upmarket developments in established suburbs by demolishing homes he apparently doesn’t own - leaving the rightful property owner out of pocket and minus a home. VO: In 2016 this development was advertised in Stella Street. Maynard van der Merwe was going to buy one of the units – part of the sale would include his existing home in Groenkloof. He spoke to us from the Eastern Cape. MAYNARD: The idea was when I moved into my new house, he would take over this house. VO: While Van der Merwe was out of town, he received these pictures from a friend – Erigh Stewart demolished his house . MAYNARD: He took possession of it, he broke it down without my permission, DEVI: After all this – you don’t have a house – not here and not on the street MAYNARD: it’s depressing…. // because he wanted me to transfer this property to him and I said – no ways! Because if I do then I would have paid you fully and I ‘ve only got a half built house in Stella Street VO: Van der Merwe is down at least R1.7 million, with no home. CASSELS: // he is an untouchable, no one is able to stop // I don’t’ think people that lost money will get anywhere // he’s got nothing – his company is always just a shell, he doesn’t even own a concrete mixer HENNIE: if you have a court order against a company that has nothing – you might just as well not have court order. VO: The NHBRC is a regulatory body of the home building industry that aims to protect the rights of housing consumers. Joubert, Cassells and Fleischman lodged complaints with the NBHRC last year that are still pending. Advocate Jakobus Swanepoel is one of the NHBRC’s prosecutors. D – giving builders far too much time to get away ADV SWANEPOEL// Does not benefit the housing consumers where they cannot actively help – try to close loop holes VO: In the Cassells’ case there are multiple counts in the charge sheet against Stewart’s company. D- Criminal action? ADV SWANEPOEL// Yes – issues of fraudulent occupation certifcate , plubming, engineer credential used fraudulent – internal investigation, referred to police services VO: In the Dawn Road case, the structural shortcomings were not picked up by NHBRC inspectors. JOUBERT: // they respond // to say they are backlogged with claims and that we should be patient. ADV SWANEPOEL: NOt adequately dEVI: Chasing for too long. VO: Du Plessis believes people should pursue the case against Stewart, criminally. HENNIE: // you can hide, but you can’t run away for ever. // no one above the law – not even erigh stewart DEVI: What do you want to see happen? CASSELS: justice, Devi just justice JOUBERT: // I’d like to see Erigh in jail, tomorrow and I’d like to throw the key away

CASSELLS : // the house was nowhere near finished – so, I didn’t pay, I said there’s no house, no payment. // the contract says that at the stage of completion then you pay. UPSOUND UNDERCOVER: ERIGH: There’s a lot of clients complain this builder did this, the developer did this, // VO: But in the Cassells’ case it was more about what the developer didn’t do. CASSELS: Kitchen not done, has been started, //no red brick, no guttering, we had our own electrician come and test the system – we found 5 plug not earthed,// the geyser was not earthed. LINK: The Marais Street owners were lucky – despite the headaches, they got a mostly finished property – here at Dawn Street – just over R2 million a pop – all the owners have to show for it. DEVI: what’s it like looking at this? JOUBERT: it’s heartbreaking, it’s heartbreaking and knowing that this is actually worth nothing VO: Neil Joubert bought into this development – this is what he expected – and three years later – this – is what he got. JOUBERT: contractually we agreed upon a pitched titled roof //the roof was wrong, it wasn’t according to plan, //– in the title deed it says that you may not construct a chromadeck roof. VO: Besides the roof - experts found that there were serious structural issues resulting in cracks in the foundations and structures. JOUBERT: // The house was built outside of SANS tolerances – which meant that the whole structure was void and couldn’t be signed off by an engineer VO: Joubert took the matter to arbitration and won – he was awarded just under R1.7 million rand because the house needs to be demolished. More than a year later, Stewart has not paid a cent. Joubert’s neighbour, Christian Fleischman is in the same boat - except he claims, that Stewart fraudulently put through three payment requests totalling just over R650 000, against his building bond with Standard Bank. Those payments were over and above the first building claim Fleischman actually signed – the amount was just over R215 000 . DEVI: Who’s signature is on those documents? CHRIS: I don’t know// I only signed one form, I didn’t sign the rest. VO: We had a forensic handwriting analyst look at the signatures. The three signatures on the payment requests submitted to the bank by Stewart’s company – are in fact forgeries according to the handwriting expert. Andrew van der Hoven is head of Home Loans at Standard Bank. DEVI: // my question is how do you as the bank pick something like this. ANDREW: You will see that the signatures are very similar. But the point is we don't have handwriting experts looking at them. Unfortunately INT2 M9 // we would pick it up in the phone call. VO: Fleischman did receive a call from the bank to authorise. CHRIS: The person who called us from the bank asked if they should proceed to make payment, they didn’t ask if we are the ones who submitted the claims, that is two different statement DEVI: proceed with payment – you said yes CHRIS: I thought maybe it was related to the first payment, //, I didn’t know they were actually receiving other progress payment requests. DEVI: Where does this leave the Fleischmans? ANDREW: Unfortunately F still release the payment and in the final call still Confirm the previous payments made. VO: Fleischman is still liable for the entire bond and interest. But it’s not just unsuspecting home buyers who Stewart allegedly leaves out of pocket – some sub-contracts claim they were not paid. OCKERT: Part of his MO is to stretch as a contractor and not pay you at the end. VO: Ockert van den Heever’s company VDH Construction did work for Stewart on multiple sites – while payments were forth coming at first, it dried up and the company was owed over R4 million rand at one time. OCKERT: // – we all basically took a hit because we didn’t get paid by Stewart and his company. VO: In a letter to the Dawn Road owners - Stewart seemingly placed the blame on VDH – but the company was never responsible for structural work on this site – the accusations included fraudulent invoicing and bad workmanship - allegations Van den Heever strongly denies. Stewart also questioned VDH’s registration with the national home builders registration council. OCKERT: it was never a requirement in any one of our contracts.// We are commercial contractors// He can // try to badmouth us – but the fact is he didn’t pay. UPSOUND UNDERCOVER ERIGH: We heard all these rumours, and everybody said stuff, and I said prove it and nobody could prove it. VO: Suspecting that we were filming him, after 40 minutes, Erigh closed the door and confronted our operative. UPSOUND UNDERCOVER: ERIGH: Nicky, Where are you from? VO: After our operative left, Stewart sent these messages: Subsequently, we made multiple attempts to interview Stewart – telephonically and by email. UPSOUND DEVI:….we really want him to do the Interview. VO: In the end, he declined an on-camera interview and refused to answer questions in writing stating the information related to a harassment-matter currently in court . He also ironically accused us of being underhanded. While Erigh Stewart was convicted of fraud and theft in the nineties, we tracked down 36 people that were owed over 17 million rand by Stewart and his associated companies from Bloemfontein to Jeffery’s Bay and Pretoria. Attorney Hennie du Plessis has consulted with some of Stewart’s upset clients and sub-contractors. dEVI: are we talking who does have a def criminal MO - HENNIE: yes –same Mo is being followed // he signs agreements – never preforms in terms of agreement DEVI: Many companies – complicate thinks HENNIE: it doesn’t matter which entities is that - // if you lift the corporate veil who are you going to find – mr erigh stewart. VO: But it appears Stewart is also in the business of threatening those who challenge him. CASSELLS: //he publically said I will kill mr cassells. UPSOUND UNDERCOVER: ERIGH // I am not the forgiving kind of person – when you slander, when you steal from me // when I am ready then I will bite, VO: Stewart also has a reputation for litigating – Van den Heever believes it’s a stalling tactic, but his company was up for the fight. OCKERT // he knows when you go into a fight it’s going to take a long time or you might give up during the course of the fight – which we never did // we basically won every single one of those cases – so he then had to settle with us – which he also never did in full. VO: Stewart signed over a property worth just over R3 million rand to VDH – he still owes around R1.2 million in related costs . But business seems to be booming with multiple developments on The Stewart Family Group’s website on offer. LINK: Erigh stewart secures prime property for his upmarket developments in established suburbs by demolishing homes he apparently doesn’t own - leaving the rightful property owner out of pocket and minus a home. VO: In 2016 this development was advertised in Stella Street. Maynard van der Merwe was going to buy one of the units – part of the sale would include his existing home in Groenkloof. He spoke to us from the Eastern Cape. MAYNARD: The idea was when I moved into my new house, he would take over this house. VO: While Van der Merwe was out of town, he received these pictures from a friend – Erigh Stewart demolished his house . MAYNARD: He took possession of it, he broke it down without my permission, DEVI: After all this – you don’t have a house – not here and not on the street MAYNARD: it’s depressing…. // because he wanted me to transfer this property to him and I said – no ways! Because if I do then I would have paid you fully and I ‘ve only got a half built house in Stella Street VO: Van der Merwe is down at least R1.7 million, with no home. CASSELS: // he is an untouchable, no one is able to stop // I don’t’ think people that lost money will get anywhere // he’s got nothing – his company is always just a shell, he doesn’t even own a concrete mixer HENNIE: if you have a court order against a company that has nothing – you might just as well not have court order. VO: The NHBRC is a regulatory body of the home building industry that aims to protect the rights of housing consumers. Joubert, Cassells and Fleischman lodged complaints with the NBHRC last year that are still pending. Advocate Jakobus Swanepoel is one of the NHBRC’s prosecutors. D – giving builders far too much time to get away ADV SWANEPOEL// Does not benefit the housing consumers where they cannot actively help – try to close loop holes VO: In the Cassells’ case there are multiple counts in the charge sheet against Stewart’s company. D- Criminal action? ADV SWANEPOEL// Yes – issues of fraudulent occupation certifcate , plubming, engineer credential used fraudulent – internal investigation, referred to police services VO: In the Dawn Road case, the structural shortcomings were not picked up by NHBRC inspectors. JOUBERT: // they respond // to say they are backlogged with claims and that we should be patient. ADV SWANEPOEL: NOt adequately dEVI: Chasing for too long. VO: Du Plessis believes people should pursue the case against Stewart, criminally. HENNIE: // you can hide, but you can’t run away for ever. // no one above the law – not even erigh stewart DEVI: What do you want to see happen? CASSELS: justice, Devi just justice JOUBERT: // I’d like to see Erigh in jail, tomorrow and I’d like to throw the key away

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): A convicted fraudster rakes in millions of rands for residential developments that never seems to materialize leaving clients out of pocket and their home owner dreams shattered - are we dealing with
metadata.Summary: From Jeffery’s Bay to Kuruman to Bloemfontein and most recently Pretoria – Erigh Stewart’s victims are out of pocket and furious – they were promised modern residential developments – parted with hundreds of thousands of rands and were left with half built property and some with land if they were lucky or worst case scenario – they get sweet nothing. His cons allegedly range from duping home buyers to scamming potential investors to even forging bank documents to get payouts his clients will be held liable for. We uncover Erigh Stewart’s trail of dodgy deals.
metadata.Further information: I have a list of 39 people that have lost over R18 million to Erigh Stewart plus an additional 21 people still to contact that have had run ins with the Stewart Group. I’ll call everyone personally and make a list that we can reference in the piece. UNDERCOVER I’ve got 40 minutes of undercover footage – I posed as an interested buyer. Erigh explains he’s had troubles with some developments, contractors and problem clients that have harassed him – at the end he turns on me realizing I was filming him and he intimidates me. He traced my number plate and sent three threatening messages: “Nice try now it is my turn” “Hope you enjoyed your little film that you made” “Hi Nicolene Celest Troll i think it is very sad that you pretend to be a client while working for Cart Banche .My family was harrassed by various people fake facebook pages and profiles.It is your job to find stories but i will take this matter up with legal council as the one woman already have a harassment order and open criminal case against her.” THIS IS HIS MO – HE INTIMIDATES AND LETIGATES. We approached Erigh for interview, I got Devi to call him – we recorded the audio. He basically says it’s smear campaign but he’ll consult with his lawyers – we then received a legal letter saying he won’t do an interview because of my underhanded behavior. THIS IS NOT AN ISSUE – it’s like he declined an interview at the end. We have him on camera in the undercover, we also have a confront style interview with Standard Bank related to one of the case studies. PRETORIA DEVELOPMENTS DRAMA 1. CLUB WILLA - NO HOUSES, JUST A WALL AND GUARD HOUSE - PREVIOUS HOUSE FLATTENED – ORIGINAL OWNER MRS DE BEER STILL BELIEVES SHE’ll GET A NEW UNIT… SHAME… 2. CORNER BESEMBESSIE STREEET & DR SWANEPOEL ROAD - SOME BUILDINGS, NOT FINISHED - LEGAL CASE WITH LAND OWNER – AT VAN WYK 3. STELLA STREET - SOME HALF BUILT BUILDINGS, NOT FINISHED - LEGAL ISSUE WITH LAND OWNER – PROPERTY HAS NOT BEEN TRANSFERRED, LAND OWNER LIVES IN CONGO. 4. DAWN STREET (FLEISCHMAN CASE) - HALF BUILT BUILDINGS, NOT FINISHED - VDH HAVE INSTITUTED BUILDER’s LIEN AGAINST PROPERTY - LAND OWNED BY CLIENTS 5. MARAIS STREET - GOT HOUSES – BUT NOT COMPLETE, NOT IN LINE WITH PLANS – OWNERS HAD TO PAY OTHER CONTRACTORS TO COMPLETE - 3 UNITS OWNED BY INDIVIDUALS, FOURTH UNIT WAS SIGNED OVER TO VDH CONSTRUCTION IN LIEU OF PAYMENT FROM ERIGH 6. FLROENCE RIBEIRO AVENUE - MR MAYNARD, A PENSIONER, WAS PROMISED A UNIT IN EXCHANGED FOR HIS LAND – HIS HOUSE WAS FLATTENED AND HE PAID IN R450k TOWARDS THE NEW UNIT TO BE BUILT ON HIS LAND – HE HAS NOTHING - NO STRUCTURES AT THIS TAGE – JUST A WALL AND A GUARD HOUSE 7. THE EMBASSY - NO STRUCTURES, JUST WALL - ONE CLIENT, TEUNS WILLEMSE RECENTLY GOT HIS MONEY BACK ***** I HAVE PHOTOS OF ALL PROPERTIES – WE CAN GO VISIT SOME OF THESE TO GET FOOTAGE. CASE STUDIES I intend on using three cases – all with strong legal arguments – two have already won their cases in court. 1. ALLEN BRITTON Allen Britton invested R1 450 000 with a promised return of R900 000 – they had a contract – Erigh was in breach – Allen took him to court and won – he has a court order for R2.5 million against Erigh from September 2018 – Erigh is meant to make monthly installments – he hasn’t. 2. CHRIS FLEISHMAN 2016 – 2017 transaction – still on going – still no property. Bought land at Dawn Street in Lynwood – the amount was R2450 000 – this would include the land and the building of the house. R900 000 for the land – R1 550 000 for the building. The Fleischman’s signed the loan withdrawal with the bank for the R900 000 for the land which has been transferred on their name. After this – there were four withdrawals against the Fleischman’s Standard Bank loan – THEY DID NOT SIGN THESE WITHDRAWAL – THEY SAY THEIR SIGNATURES WERE FORGED. STANDARD BANK CAN’T PRODUCE THE ORGINAL DOCUMENTS. The building is half built, what is there doesn’t match the plans that were approved and lodged with the bank – so in any case the bank the should not have signed off and allowed the payments to go through. The roof is incorrect and illegal in terms of Lynwood building regulations, the windows that have been installed are alos incorrect. STANDARD BANK HAS SOME EXPLAINING TO DO. Currently Standard Bank are demanding bond payments from the Fleischman’s for a property that is not complete and illegal. In addition, the construction company VDH Construction have instituted a builder’s lien claim against the property – Erigh put the Fleischman’s property down as collateral with the construction company – they have now instituted a claim agains the property. This has happened to the other three unit owners at Dawn Street as well. Niel Joubert legally challenged Standard Bank and won – but signed a non-disclosure agreement – the bond was cancelled. 3. VDH CONSTRUCTION This company has also won a case against Erigh – the result was that he had to sign over one of the units in one of the only developments that he completed – all be it not according to plan and there was work outstanding that the home owners had to foot the bill for. There was a quantity surveyor that testified against Erigh in this case and was received death threats afterwards. ADDITIONAL INTEVIEWS - GROUP LEADER The person Erigh mentions he has the harassment order against is an estate agent who worked on marketing one of the developments and loaned him R280k – she and her husband realized something was not right and started warning clients. She has dug up a lot of history on Erigh and would be great as a hidden identity interview (pending her harassment case) to give a bigger picture of the extent of Erigh’s alleged fraud. She traced cases back to 1996. - STANDARD BANK - NHBRC – Erigh has undervalued a lot of the properties and they have had multiple complaints about him – but appear to not do much…. - Maybe a legal expert – to comment on the challenges with pursuing him criminally because he changes companies regularly – and the cases are dealt with individually on a civial bases and are not getting addressed criminally. I think it might actually be better to leave out the Group leader and just do the lawyer.
